source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.campus_mw_context: ASH2 is a 226K SQFT, two-story, Cologix-owned facility under construction at 21673 Beaumeade Circle in Ashburn, Virginia. With 51 MW of available power capacity, ASH2 is designed for high-density workloads. The facility enables flexible deployment across liquid-cooled and air-cooled environments, supported by dual independent utility feeds, block-redundant power architecture and a prime location in Data Center Alley — the world’s most interconnected data center market.

reading.body:
Cologix ASH2 is a 51 MW campus under construction in Ashburn, Virginia, with two addresses on Beaumeade Circle and a two-story, 226,000 square foot building the operator owns. The published specification says it is designed for high-density workloads and supports both liquid-cooled and air-cooled deployment, which matters because the cooling choice determines what accelerator generation a building can host, not just how much power it draws. The 51 MW figure is available power capacity, not a measurement of what is installed today, and the page does not publish a construction completion date, an energized load, or any tenant.

Translating that figure into physical scale requires an assumption the operator does not make. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 51 MW of critical IT load is roughly 1,275 racks, from 51,000 kW divided by 40 kW per rack. At a lower 15 kW per rack, the same power supports about 3,400 racks. Neither number is Cologix's claim, and the real count depends on rack density, cooling design, and how much of the 51 MW is reserved for mechanical overhead rather than IT equipment. The dual independent utility feeds and block-redundant power architecture qualify the campus to keep serving load through a single utility failure, which is the baseline qualification for training clusters that cannot tolerate interruption. The liquid and air cooling support qualifies it to host both current-generation air-cooled racks and denser liquid-cooled racks in the same building, without naming which hardware that would be.

In Virginia, this site is one of 376 mapped facilities but only 29 with a published megawatt figure, and its 51 MW ranks 30th by published capacity in a state whose published total is 2,563.4 MW. That rank is a statement about disclosure, not about size: most Virginia facilities publish nothing, so a campus can be large and still absent from the ranking. What the ranking does show is that ASH2 sits just outside the top of the state's disclosed capacity, in the same market as the largest published campuses, and that its 51 MW is roughly two percent of all megawatts Virginia operators have chosen to publish. For a reader asking whether this campus matters to AI, the answer is that it adds a disclosed, high-density, dual-fed 51 MW to the one market where interconnectivity is deepest, and that the binding constraint on whether it trains models is not the building but the power and the chips that arrive after construction ends.
